clue.text: Gorilla has to consume fruit outside

indicators.note: the fruit sits outside, wrapping round the word for consuming

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A gorilla tucking into fruit, peel and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. 'Gorilla' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the primates classed as great apes, alongside chimpanzees and orangutans.

clue.text: A pivotal aid at sea?

parts.note: pivotal suggests crucial, but literally it means turning on pivots, the device keeping a ship's compass level

explanation.surface: Something crucial that helps sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pivotal' usually means vital; here it means mounted on pivots.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimbal is a set of pivoted rings that keeps a ship's compass or chronometer horizontal as the vessel rolls.

clue.text: He may have set features at work

definitions.text: He may have set features at work

parts.words: He may have set features at work
parts.note: set features sounds like a fixed face, but means arranged articles in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A man wearing a fixed expression at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set features' suggests a stern face; in newspapers features are articles, which this person sets out.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper or magazine decides which feature articles appear.

clue.text: The initial question is put with vigour and detachment

indicators.note: initial picks out just the first letter of the word The

parts.note: to ask is to put a question
force means vigour or power

explanation.surface: A first question delivered forcefully yet with cool detachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detachment' looks like aloofness, but means a military unit; 'with' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a body of troops sent off for a special purpose, which is what this unit is.

clue.text: His rapport with me may lead to a life of pleasure

indicators.note: may lead to suggests the letters can be led into a new form, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man's rapport with the speaker could bring a pleasurable life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the fodder words HIS RAPPORT and ME and is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Hamlet, means a pursuit of pleasure and ease, often heading to ruin.

clue.text: One's lucky in races beyond a mile

indicators.note: the race meeting comes beyond, that is after, the abbreviation for a mile

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for mile
Ascot is a famous English racecourse and its race meeting

explanation.surface: Someone striking lucky at the races after a mile-long run.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse near Windsor, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good luck, so it is a lucky one.

clue.text: Wool drops a point in the market

indicators.note: drops means the wool lets go of one letter, the compass point

parts.note: angora is wool from the Angora goat or rabbit
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The price of wool falling a point at market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops a point' sounds like a price fall, but removes N from ANGORA; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the agora was the public square used as a marketplace.

clue.text: Enormous deficit in solid fuel

indicators.note: in places the shortfall inside the word for solid fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A vast shortfall in the coal supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means immense, like the giant ancient statue called the Colossus.

clue.text: When stream enters the river it provides excitement

indicators.note: enters says the small stream goes into the other words

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: The thrill of a stream joining a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is only a link word here. 'it provides' makes the definition a description of something that excites.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a suspenseful novel or film designed to excite its audience.

clue.text: Chief means for a yacht to travel by sea?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the word for sea sits next to the word for travelling

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
to sail is to travel over water

explanation.surface: A question about how best to get a yacht moving across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief' looks like part of the wordplay giving MAIN, but MAIN comes from 'sea'; the whole clue nearly defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsail is the principal sail on a yacht, its chief means of propulsion.

clue.text: Delivery man?

parts.note: suggests a postman or courier, but in cricket a delivery is a ball sent down to the batsman

explanation.surface: Someone who brings parcels to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball sent down is called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket player who sends balls down at the batsman makes deliveries, so is a delivery man.

clue.text: Full board in a way

parts.note: thorough means full or complete
board means meals provided, as in bed and board, which is fare

explanation.surface: Full board offered at an inn, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full board' looks like a hotel booking, but splits into two pieces; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public way through a place.

clue.text: A backward idiot, apart from all else

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for idiot from end to start

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A slow-witted fool keeping himself apart from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like it describes the idiot, but it turns his letters round to give LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing apart from others, distant and detached, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: What the listener does in actual practice

indicators.note: in places the listener's action inside the word for actual

parts.note: real means actual
a listener hears

explanation.surface: How a listener behaves during a real practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a play or concert before the real performance.

clue.text: Push lever to gets news handout

definitions.meaning: a release you press: a catch or lever that frees something when pushed
an official statement issued to the newspapers

explanation.surface: An instruction to push a lever to get the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'gets' is ungrammatical here and appears to be a misprint for 'get', as printed in the paper; 'to gets' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement handed out to journalists by an organisation is the standard term for an official news handout.

clue.text: Crude oil in a USA state

indicators.note: crude means raw or unrefined, so the letters are taken as rough material to be reworked

explanation.surface: Raw petroleum found in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' looks like one phrase, but 'Crude' signals an anagram of OIL IN A USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the states of the USA, on the Gulf of Mexico, itself an oil producer.

clue.text: Northerner gives berth on board to one of the crew

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the berth goes inside the steamship letters

parts.note: with 'on', board is a ship; SS stands for steamship
a cot is a sailor's bed or berth
a man is a member of a crew

explanation.surface: A northerner offering a crewman a bunk aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the usual way 'on board' puts letters inside; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotsman comes from Scotland, in the north of Britain, so is a northerner.

clue.text: Liqueur made in top Eastern state

indicators.note: made suggests something constructed, so these letters are assembled anew
top picks the first letter of Eastern, at the head of this down entry

explanation.surface: A liqueur produced in a leading eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes E from 'Eastern'; IN, E and STATE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Scornful of fashionable costume put on

indicators.note: fashionable hints at fashioning, so the letters of the following words are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a modish outfit someone has put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like a description of the costume, but it signals an anagram of COSTUME PUT ON; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being contemptuous means showing scorn or disdain for someone or something.

clue.text: Sort of school French king goes up to after short month

indicators.note: after places the French king behind the short month

parts.note: Jun is the short form of June

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch visiting school after a brief month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns ROI into IOR; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior school teaches younger children, typically aged seven to eleven in Britain.

clue.text: Well acquainted with the metric system

definitions.meaning: taken as metre in poetry: put into lines with metre

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with kilograms and metres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metric system' suggests measures but here means poetic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Versed means skilled or knowledgeable, and also put into poetic lines with a regular metre.

clue.text: River lighter may transfer the ashes

definitions.note: describes a thing, a noun phrase in sense: an England-Australia game that can win or lose the Ashes trophy

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, famous for trout fishing
a match is a lighter of fires

explanation.surface: A river boat or lighter carrying away someone's cremated ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia; 'lighter' looks like a barge on the river but is a fire-starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes series is decided by international five-day games, so one of these can see the trophy change hands.

clue.text: Right, or in French, wrong

indicators.note: in tells us the word or sits inside the French word for wrong

parts.note: mal is French for bad or wrong

explanation.surface: A question of right and wrong, posed in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral, as an adjective, describes what is right or ethically good.

clue.text: Relish a piece of impudence

definitions.meaning: a condiment or savoury accompaniment to food
cheek or insolent talk, as in 'none of your lip'

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark seen as something to savour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a condiment poured on food and, informally, cheek or insolence.

clue.text: Adult scholar with true disposition

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement means the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A grown-up academic with an honest temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals an arrangement of TRUE into TURE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mature, as an adjective, means fully grown or adult.

clue.text: Girl to sign for earnings

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A young woman being signed up for paid work.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are the fixed regular payments people earn from employment.

clue.text: Poverty to the French produces hostility

parts.note: need means want or poverty
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Hardship among the French breeding resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle is informal British usage for antagonism or ill feeling, as in a needle match.

clue.text: Excluded lawyers' right to be in action

indicators.note: to be in tells us the lawyers and the right go inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
the Bar is the body of barristers, collectively lawyers

explanation.surface: Barristers barred from taking part in legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks like a lawsuit, fitting the lawyers, but here is simply a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be debarred is to be shut out or banned from something, so excluded.
